harrat-mujtaba:1-1.t: The preposition «من أهل» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «كفروا»; «منفكيِّن» here: the khabar (predicate) of كان, from the complete (tāmm) انفكَّ; and the genitive interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) «حتى تأتيهم» is attached to «منفكين».

harrat-mujtaba:2-2.t: «رسول»: badal (substitute) of {الْبَيِّنَةُ}, a substitute of the whole for the whole by way of hyperbole: He made the Messenger the very البنية [Translator's note: so in the source; evidently البينة (the clear proof) is meant]; the preposition «من الله» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) رسول; and the clause «يتلو» is a naʿt (adjective) of «رسول».

harrat-mujtaba:3-3.t: (فيها كتب قيمة) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is a naʿt (adjective) of {صُحُفًا}.

harrat-mujtaba:4-4.t: The clause «وما تفرَّق» is conjoined to the clause {لَمْ يَكُنِ الَّذِينَ}; the preposition «من بعد» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «تفرَّق»; «ما»: maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun), and the interpreted maṣdar is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

harrat-mujtaba:5-5.t: The clause «وما أُمروا» is conjoined to the clause «ما تفرق»; the genitive interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) «ليعبدوا» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أمروا»; «مخلصين»: ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «يعبدوا»; the preposition «له» is attached to «مخلصين»; «الدين»: mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the active participle; «حنفاء»: a second ḥāl; and the clause «وذلك دين» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:6-6.t: The preposition «من أهل» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «كفروا»; «خالدين»: ḥāl from the latent (mustatir) pronoun in the khabar (predicate) of «إنَّ»; «هم»: pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl); and the clause «أولئك شر» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:7-7.t: The clause «أولئك هم خير» is the khabar (predicate) of إنَّ, and «هم» is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl).

harrat-mujtaba:8-8.t: The preposition «عند» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the maṣdar (verbal noun) in «جزاؤهم»; the clause «جزاؤهم جنات» is resumptive; the clause «تجري» is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), since جنات is annexed to the proper name «عدن» and so acquired definiteness; the clause «رضي الله عنهم» is resumptive, and likewise the clause «ذلك لمن خشي».
